generatedProse.concept-context: Tasks across the School of Sport rarely have one right route. A session can be planned several ways, a rehab programme built on different principles, a report structured in more than one order, a research question approached with different designs. Thinking flexibly means producing a few of these approaches before you commit, then watching how your chosen one goes. If it stalls, you amend it or switch, rather than forcing an approach that is not working. A coach weighs drills, a therapist weighs protocols, a manager weighs strategies, but the habit is shared.
generatedProse.worked-example:
Two sport coaching students are set the same demanding session plan with a tight deadline.

Tom picks the first session structure that comes to mind and commits to it. Half way through planning, the drills clearly do not build towards the session aim, but Tom pushes on the same way, hoping more detail will fix it. Time runs out with little that works. There was never a second structure to turn to.

Amara starts by jotting three ways the session could be organised, then tries the most promising one. Seeing the drills fail to build towards the aim, Amara stops, returns to the list, and switches to a structure that fits the players better. The session plan gets finished, because a change of course was always available.

Both students worked hard. Only Amara generated options and stayed ready to adapt, turning a stall into a switch rather than a dead end.
generatedProse.summary: Thinking flexibly in the School of Sport has two parts: generating several approaches to a task before you commit, and monitoring your chosen approach so you can adapt or switch when it is not working. You can now produce more than one way into a session, a programme or a report, watch how an approach is going, and change course with control rather than pushing on regardless. The next lesson turns creativity onto the material itself, bringing imagination to analysis.

check.body: In the worked example, what let Amara realise her first approach was not working?

items.text: She kept checking, as she worked, whether the session structure was getting her anywhere.
She waited until the deadline to review the whole session plan.
She asked Tom what structure to use.
She had chosen only one structure from the start.

feedback.correct: That's right. Monitoring the work as she went is what let Amara spot the stall in time to switch.
feedback.incorrectNotFinal: Not quite. What was Amara doing while she worked that Tom was not?
feedback.incorrectFinal: Amara kept checking, as she worked, whether her structure was getting anywhere. That monitoring revealed the stall in time to switch.
